accused_victim_relationship: Business relationship (film distributor and theatre owner); accused alleged prior dispute over release of film 'Pokari'
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 s.138 (presumption under s.139)
evidence_type: Documentary (cheque, bank return memo, legal notice) with statutory presumption under s.139
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.138 NI Act; fine Rs 5,55,000 or five months simple imprisonment in default
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision allowed; concurrent convictions set aside and accused acquitted
offence_finally_established: Dishonour of cheque under Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
neutral_facts: The complainant, who owns a theatre, alleges that he advanced a loan of five lakh rupees to the accused on 20 May 2006 to support the production of a Tamil film, and that she promised to repay it on the film's release. When repayment was not made, the accused issued a cheque for five lakh rupees, drawn on a State Bank of Mysore branch, on 16 January 2007. The complainant presented the cheque through his bank on the same day. The bank returned it on 18 January 2007 with the remark 'Stop Payment'. The complainant then sent a legal notice on 27 January 2007 to the accused's office and residential addresses. The residential notice was duly received, while the office notice was returned marked 'Absent-Information delivered'. The accused did not pay or respond. The accused's position is that she was only a name lender to a film distribution firm run by her husband. She denied taking any loan and said the cheque was an old security cheque given in 1999 against an earlier loan, which the complainant had supposedly misplaced and later misused. The cheque bore a printed date of 1999 on its leaf, though it was filled in with the 2007 date. The cheque and the signature on it were not disputed.
financial_property_loss: Rs 5,00,000 (amount of the dishonoured cheque, representing the alleged loan)
motive: alleged: repayment of Rs 5 lakh loan advanced on 20-05-2006 (complainant's case)
key_evidence_accepted: Undisputed cheque and signature; dishonour for 'stop payment'; accused's knowledge of presentation inferred from the stop-payment instruction
witness_credibility: Court found the accused's 1999 security-cheque story unworthy of credit and unsupported by evidence; the High Court's reliance on the printed date alone was not conclusive
post_offence_conduct: Court inferred from instructing bank to stop payment that accused knew the cheque was being presented
trial_duration: offence: not given (cheque dated 16-01-2007; dishonoured 18-01-2007); trial judgment: not given (Magistrate); Fast Track Court: 22.01.2011; High Court: 22-07-2011; Supreme Court: 28-04-2015
legal_representation: Accused (respondent): Kiran Suri, Apurva Upamanyu, Dr. Vipin Gupta. Appellant (complainant): Rajesh Mahale, Krutin R. Joshi. No State counsel appears.
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the court as a procedural lapse; the Supreme Court held the High Court wrongly placed the burden of proof on the complainant
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted. Fast Track Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld. High Court (revision): concurrent findings reversed, accused acquitted. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction restored.
defence_argument: Not stated in Supreme Court arguments; accused's case at trial was that a 1999 security cheque was misused by the complainant for revenge
legal_principle_applied: Rebuttable presumption under s.139 NI Act; once cheque and signature are admitted the burden shifts to the accused to disprove a legally recoverable debt
